answers.answer: Stand a visible ID in your chosen color, take the matching Voting set, remove target cards for colors not playing, and retain your Ambush card. Put the Gold deck face down and deal four central Gold Bar cards with values hidden.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: There is no turn order. Choices can change until reveal. Once everyone has chosen, all reveal simultaneously.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: No majority is required: the greatest vote total determines the Target. Red alone is Target because three is the highest count.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: Both tied Targets are eliminated. A non-Target voter who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and is not eliminated for voting outside the Target group.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: No. A player who did not vote for a Target is also eliminated, even when nobody voted for that player. Green voted outside the Target group and is eliminated.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: Ambush adds no vote. Red and Yellow each have one vote and are tied Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives its successful Ambush and can retaliate only against Yellow, who voted for Red. Pink voted for tied Target Yellow and survives, leaving Red and Pink.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: The ambusher survives and eliminates exactly one of the players who voted for them. They neither eliminate every voter nor choose someone who did not vote for them.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: The Ambush fails and that player eliminates themselves.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: The round continues with another conspiracy and vote among the four survivors. It ends when the resolved vote leaves one, two or no survivors.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. Four bars are four cards, not four points; each Gold Bar is worth 3, 4 or 5 points.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: They must hold a Final Showdown. Each receives Share, Steal and Grab One & Go, may discuss intentions, secretly chooses one card face down, and reveals simultaneously with the other finalist.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: Nobody receives the central bars. Every player not involved in that final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck; participants in that final vote receive none. Leave the four central bars and add no new central gold next round.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two of the four central Gold Bar cards.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: The Share player receives no bars and the Steal player receives all four.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: Grab One & Go receives one bar and Steal receives three.

answers.answer: Each takes one central bar. Leave the other two central and deal just two new central bars for the next round.

answers.answer: Both finalists receive nothing. Each other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round rather than replacing them.

answers.answer: Check at round end after Gold Bar awards. The threshold is 25 points with 6–9 players and 24 with 10–12. When several qualify, the highest total wins.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: The tied players conduct another Final Showdown, repeating until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. If no winner ends the game, every player returns next round: stand all IDs upright again.
answers.novelty: Distinct procedural rule, source-defined outcome branch, or consequential voting interaction.

answers.answer: Conspire for no longer than roughly a minute and a half. Any overt or covert means is allowed, including texting and showing Voting cards. The game owner asks players for their final decisions before voting.
answers.novelty: Conspiracy duration, unrestricted communication and transition to voting were not tested by the seed.

answers.answer: Choose the Voting card matching the ID color of the person you want to eliminate and place it face down in front of you. Play your own Ambush card instead of choosing another player’s card if you suspect you are the Target.
answers.novelty: Tests legal action/card identity and face-down placement, rather than reveal timing or Ambush outcome.

answers.answer: Knock over eliminated players’ IDs. Surviving IDs stay standing; only survivors participate in the next vote.
answers.novelty: Tests the procedural state indicator, absent from seed question on returning upright next round.

answers.answer: Deal four new central Gold Bar cards for the next round, keeping their values hidden. Refill to four only if play continues; the retained-pot exceptions apply when bars were left behind.
answers.novelty: Tests normal replenishment branch; seed tests retained-pot exceptions but never asks ordinary replenishment.

answers.answer: No. Blue remains the Target from the tally, even though Ambush protects Blue. Purple is not promoted to Target; players who did not vote for Blue are eliminated. Blue also chooses one player who voted for Blue to eliminate.
answers.novelty: Tests consequential interaction of target determination with later Ambush protection: no retally or promotion of runner-up.

answers.answer: The tied players must conduct another Final Showdown until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. The booklet provides only a two-player Showdown procedure and no arrangement for three or more tied players. A specific multiway procedure is unresolved in this source; do not invent one.
answers.novelty: Explicitly tests a material source limitation beyond the seed’s exactly-two-player tie. This does not resolve the missing procedure or count as a full procedural PASS.

answers.answer: Yes. Double Steal gives every player outside the pair one Gold Bar from the deck while the finalists get nothing. The tie instruction continues until any single player at the table has the highest Gold point total, so an outside player who thereby becomes the sole highest wins.
answers.novelty: Tests an exception to treating original tied finalists as the only eligible winners: tie-resolution compensation can make an outsider the single highest player at the table.
